column1: # context | listener turn and specific outcome | reply achieving outcome | plausible competing reply
booking|The host says “Fifty, right?” You need fifteen seats.|Fifteen, please. One five.|Yes, five zero.
invite|A visitor asks “Is anyone sitting here?” Offer the chair.|Please take this seat.|I'm keeping it for Pat.
plural|Two friends each need one bag. The clerk asks “One bag?”|Two bags, please.|One bag will do.
past|Yesterday's parcel is already packed. Your colleague asks if they should pack it.|I packed it yesterday.|I'll pack it tomorrow.
clusters|A server brings a menu. Ask for a drink first.|Could I get a drink first?|Could I get the bill first?
syllables|The driver heard a one-syllable code. Your code was Maybe.|Maybe. It has two beats.|May. That's the whole code.
startcluster|The driver repeats Ring Street. The correct name is Spring Street.|Spring Street, beginning like springtime.|Yes, Ring Street.
stress|Nobody is taking notes. Ask Sam to capture the meeting audio.|Sam, could you record this?|Sam, where is the record?
compound|Your friend sees a green-painted house. You mean the glass building for plants.|Meet me by the greenhouse with the seedlings.|Yes, the house with green paint.
longstress|A teammate asks how you learned your breathing technique. Explain how you developed it.|I learned it slowly by practising one breath at a time.|I can show you where the meeting is.
family|Someone asks who took the photograph. Identify the photographer.|Nina took it on Monday.|It shows the old bridge.
weak|A friend doubts that you can drive. Reassure them about your ability.|I CAN drive. Let me take the wheel.|I can WALK there instead.
negative|The office thinks you sent the email. You saved a draft only.|I didn't send it yet.|Yes, I sent it this morning.
aux|A friend could stay or leave. Make a clear recommendation to stay.|I think you should stay.|You could stay or leave.
pronouns|The clerk is holding the correct ticket but giving it to the wrong person.|Give HER the ticket, please.|Give him the TICKET, please.
link|Your friend dropped a key. Ask them to retrieve it.|Pick it up.|Put it down.
reduction|You agreed to meet next week. The caller repeats this week.|Next week, after the weekend.|Yes, before this weekend.
rhythm|The traveller has the destination. Give the transport and departure time.|Take the bus at nine.|The office is next to the park.
group|Invite a friend to eat after work. Keep the time and invitation together.|After work, let's get dinner.|Let's get dinner before work.
story|You walked first and ran later. A listener has the sequence backwards.|We walked first. Then we ran.|That's right, we ran before walking.
continue|You have one item left to order. The server starts to leave.|And one more thing, please.|That's everything, thanks.
smalltalk|It is warm outside. Invite the other person to join the conversation.|It's warm today. How are you finding it?|It's warm today. I have to go.
instructions|The visitor repeats right. They need the left turn after the gate.|Left after the gate, please.|Right after the gate, yes.
quote|Mia asked if it was today. Report her question.|Mia asked, “Today?”|Mia confirmed it was today.
emphasis|The listener says Mia sent the note. You sent it.|I sent the note.|Mia sent the note.
addition|Your friend packed water. They also need a coat.|Bring a coat too.|Leave the water and take a coat instead.
contrast|The clerk picks a green folder. You need a blue one.|The blue folder, please.|Yes, that green one.
topic|You have finished discussing dinner. Ask about the weekend.|By the way, what are we doing on Saturday?|Could I have another helping?
checking|Someone moves a call to noon. Check that you heard the new time.|Noon, did you say?|Shall we leave it at nine?
asking|You need the address. First find out the street.|Which street is it on?|Is the meeting today?
given|Your colleague knows you met Nina. They ask when.|We met on MONDAY.|I met NINA.
attitude|A colleague asks whether the proposed time works. Give a firm agreement.|Sure. I'll be there.|Are you sure that's the time?
